notable_absence.finding: RESOLVES a gap flagged in this batch's other extraction records: create-type-mapping.json, create-child-field.json, and create-child-mapping.json each note that no role is stated for editing a type mapping. This page - a Search-index-editing task at the same UI location (Edit an index) - names 'Search Admin' (role:fts-admin) explicitly. Whether this same role also gates the sibling mapping-editing tasks is never stated by any of them, so the absence on those pages is not fully closed, only made more likely to have the same answer.

cross_component_finding: This page also states, without naming a predicate target: 'You cannot use custom document filters with another type of type identifier on your Search index. If you select an option other than **Custom** after you have defined custom document filters, you'll lose any defined custom filters on your Search index' - a mutual-exclusivity/destructive-switch constraint among the four search:type-identifier-mode-enum values. No existing promoted predicate cleanly captures 'switching to a sibling enum value discards previously configured state for another value' (closest candidates - takesPrecedenceOver, retainedForLegacyCompatibility - both imply the wrong shape), so this was recorded here in prose rather than forced into a relation; flagged for reconciliation as a possible new predicate (e.g. discardsConfigurationOnSwitch) if this shape recurs elsewhere in the search: namespace's mode-enum family. Separately, the page states a numeric ceiling - 'You can add up to a maximum of 100 custom document filters on a single Search index' - which is a literal-valued fact (like the existing hasMinimumNodeCount/hasMinimumMemoryToDataRatio family) but for which no predicate currently exists in this exact shape (maximum count of a configuration object per index); also left unminted here rather than force-fit.
